key_insight: Microscopic residual impurities in wide-bandgap perovskite films act as degradation nucleation sites, and they can be rapidly detected with imaging plus machine learning before devices fail.
engineering_relevance: The study provides a fast, non-invasive screening workflow to rank perovskite film stability early in manufacturing, supporting scale-up of more reliable solar cells.
method: Nano-FTIR identified the chemical nature of impurity phases.
High-resolution reflected-light microscopy captured impurity patterns across films.
Machine learning quantified impurity density for rapid pre-screening and degradation tracking.
evidence_signal: Photo-stress and imaging analyses showed degradation begins at impurity-perovskite interfaces, and films with higher impurity density exhibited faster early degradation.
watch_item: Impurity-density screening is an early diagnostic, but it must be chemically validated and may not capture all other failure pathways in real device stacks.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
